mainTopic: Explaining the case of 'אם ארחץ' in the משנה about vows a husband may cancel (נדרי עינוי נפש), and explaining why רבי יוסי disagrees
overview: The משנה lists the vow 'if I bathe' (אם ארחץ) as a vow of affliction (עינוי נפש) that a husband can cancel. רבי יוסי disagrees and says such vows are not עינוי נפש. The גמרא tries to work out exactly what the woman vowed so that both views make sense. First it suggests she said bathing is forbidden to her forever if she bathes. Then she is trapped: bathing sets off a lifelong ban, and not bathing leaves her disfigured. On this reading, רבי יוסי holds she can simply not bathe, and we do not worry about the disfigurement. The גמרא objects that if this were his reason, רבי יוסי should have said 'this condition has no affliction.' So the גמרא gives a final version: she said bathing is forbidden to her forever if she bathes today. רבי יוסי holds that being unwashed for one day does not count as disfigurement, so the vow is not עינוי נפש.

steps.title: A new explanation: she forbade bathing forever if she bathes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the woman said: 'Benefit from bathing is forbidden to me forever if I bathe.' This puts her in a trap, so the husband can cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, she said: 'Bathing is קונם for me forever if I bathe.' That is why the husband can cancel it. What can she do? If she bathes, bathing becomes forbidden to her forever. If she does not bathe, she becomes unkempt and disfigured.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier explanation of 'אם ארחץ' did not work, so the גמרא offers a new picture of what the woman actually vowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both sides of the vow hurt her. Bathing triggers a lifelong ban on bathing, and not bathing leaves her dirty and disfigured. Because she is stuck either way, it counts as עינוי נפש and the husband may cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier explanation and offering a new one)
A word that makes something forbidden like a קרבן; the standard vow formula
Cancels (a husband canceling his wife's vow)
Disfigurement or unkemptness, from not washing

phrases.english: "The benefit of bathing is קונם for me

phrases.notes: Bathing even once sets off the vow, and then bathing is forbidden to her for the rest of her life.

phrases.english: Because of this, he can cancel it for her.
If she bathes, the benefit of bathing becomes forbidden to her;
if she does not bathe, she suffers disfigurement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces an earlier explanation of the משנה's case (from before this section) that was rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the vow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier explanation of what 'אם ארחץ' meant did not fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow is a lifelong ban on bathing triggered by bathing, so she is trapped either way.

steps.title: Why רבי יוסי disagrees: she can just not bathe
steps.stepSummary: Under this explanation, רבי יוסי holds the vow is not affliction, because she can avoid bathing and we do not worry about her becoming unkempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי holds: it is possible for her not to bathe, and we are not concerned about disfigurement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the new explanation by showing how רבי יוסי fits in. He sees a simple way out for her: don't bathe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי does not count disfigurement from not washing as real affliction. So she can avoid setting off the vow without suffering, and the husband cannot cancel it as עינוי נפש.

phrases.english: it is possible for her not to bathe,
and we are not concerned about disfigurement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 1's explanation by explaining רבי יוסי's dissent.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the dissenting view within the new case
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי, she can avoid the condition, so the vow is not עינוי נפש.

steps.title: Then רבי יוסי should have spoken about the condition
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוסי's point is only that she can avoid bathing, the משנה should quote him as saying 'this condition has no affliction.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the משנה teach this: רבי יוסי says, 'This condition has no affliction in it!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation in steps 1–2 by pointing to the exact words רבי יוסי uses in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 1–2, רבי יוסי's reason is about the condition ('if I bathe'), which she can easily avoid. It is not about the vow itself. But in the משנה he says 'these are not vows of affliction,' which sounds like it is about the vow. So his wording does not match this explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach (the משנה should have said)
Affliction of the self; the type of vow a husband can cancel

phrases.english: If so, let it teach this:

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַאי זֶה אֵין בּוֹ עִנּוּי נֶפֶשׁ!
phrases.english: This condition has no affliction in it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in steps 1–2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי יוסי's reason is that she can avoid bathing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reason is about the condition, so רבי יוסי's wording in the משנה should have mentioned the condition, not the vows.

steps.title: Final explanation: if I bathe today
steps.stepSummary: She said bathing is forbidden to her forever if she bathes today. רבי יוסי holds that going one day without bathing is not considered disfigurement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, she said: 'The benefit of bathing is forbidden to me forever if I bathe today.' And רבי יוסי holds that disfigurement for one day is not called disfigurement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a new version of the vow. Her vow now depends only on bathing today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the only cost of avoiding the vow is skipping one day of bathing. The argument is about whether that counts as affliction. רבי יוסי says one day of being unwashed is not disfigurement at all, so the vow is not עינוי נפש. That fits his wording, 'these are not vows of affliction.'

keyTerms.meaning: Is not called (does not count as)

steps.whatToRemember: The case of 'אם ארחץ' is a vow forbidding bathing forever if she bathes today. The תנא קמא counts even one day unwashed as affliction. רבי יוסי says one day of disfigurement is not real disfigurement.

phrases.english: "The benefit of bathing is upon me forever
phrases.notes: The word קונם is not repeated here, but it is understood, just like in step 1.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by redefining the vow.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case so that the dispute is about the affliction itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow applied to any bathing ever, so רבי יוסי's reason would only be about avoiding the condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow applies to bathing today. The argument is whether one day unwashed counts as affliction, and רבי יוסי says it does not.
